web_evidence.title: Before the Fall by Noah Hawley | Excerpt
web_evidence.note: A sustained opening excerpt narrates the Batemans and other passengers externally while moving among their histories, perceptions, and thoughts. Its generic you and we reflections do not designate a protagonist or participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Before the Fall Chapter 1-Part 1, Chapter 12 Summary & Analysis
web_evidence.note: Detailed structural analysis identifies third-person narration in both the present-day plot and past-tense backstories, with free indirect discourse across characters. It separately identifies five painting-description chapters whose you addresses the viewer, not a story protagonist.

web_evidence.title: Noah Hawley Writing Styles in Before the Fall
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly describes the novel as third-person omniscient, providing access to multiple characters before, during, and after the crash.

web_evidence.title: Before the Fall Literary Elements
web_evidence.note: Its narrator-and-point-of-view section explicitly classifies the story as third person, independently corroborating the stronger structural evidence.

person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating third person, moving omnisciently or through free indirect discourse among Scott, the passengers, investigators, and other characters. Diagnostic quote passages agree with the authorized opening and explicit structural sources. First-person forms in the quote set occur in aphorisms, attributed speech, or embedded thought, while most instances of you and we are universal address. The five painting-description chapters use you to position the reader as a viewer rather than narrating a story-specific protagonist, so they do not create sustained second-person base narration or justify ALTERNATING. The authorized prose source covers only the opening, but the whole-book and structural sources resolve that scope limitation without credible contrary evidence.
